name: ecommerce-retail
appliesTo: Marketplaces, D2C shops, food delivery, fashion, groceries. Vietnamese online selling has its own settled voice, and it is closer to a message than to a page.

address.customer: bạn is genuinely correct here, and anh/chị when the order gets serious — payment, delivery, returns.
address.self: shop, or mình. `Shop giao trong 2 ngày` is the native phrasing.
avoid: quý khách outside of invoices and legal pages

glossary.why: `ship` is the word buyers and sellers both use. The formal expansion belongs on the invoice, not the checkout button.
One settled term across the market.

wrong: thanh toán khi nhận hàng tận nơi
glossary.why: COD is understood everywhere; spell it out once on the policy page and use the short form in flow.

extraRules.why: Not wrong, but in casual retail copy people say and read `50k`. Full notation in running text reads like a receipt.
extraRules.instead: 50k in marketing and chat copy. Keep the full 50.000 ₫ on invoices, checkout totals and anything legal.
extraRules.falsePositives: Checkout and invoice strings should keep the full form — allow those explicitly.

extraRules.pattern: (chỉ còn \d+ (giây|phút)|nhanh tay kẻo hết|sắp hết hàng)
extraRules.why: Manufactured scarcity. Vietnam's consumer protection law prohibits misleading commercial information, and buyers here recognise the pattern from marketplaces already.
extraRules.instead: state the real stock number or the real deadline, or say nothing

notes: Prices: 50.000 ₫ formally, 50k in casual copy. Never a $ sign. Delivery windows day-first and 24-hour. Softeners are plentiful and correct in this register — `nha` especially, which reads southern and friendly.
